_comment: Extend Extract configuration for Planq. Loaded at runtime by api/extend_extract.py and submitted inline; nothing here is hand-authored in code. Field names and descriptions follow https://docs.extend.ai/extraction/best-practices/field-names-and-prompt-crafting. Schema rules: every primitive is nullable and every enum carries a null option, per https://docs.extend.ai/extraction/schema.
extractionRules:
You are reading an architectural permit drawing sheet for a building-code compliance review in Alberta, Canada. Treat the reader as a new employee who has never seen this drawing set.

Work in this order for every item you report:
1. Locate the label or tag on the drawing (for example a door tag D-1, a room name such as BEDROOM 2, or a dimension leader).
2. Read the associated measurement exactly as printed. Do not compute, average, scale, or infer a measurement that is not printed on the sheet.
3. Record the number and its unit separately. Never merge them into one string.

Measurement rules:
- Report the numeric magnitude in the 'value' field as a number, with no unit characters, no quotes, and no thousands separators.
- Report the unit in the 'unit' field using exactly one of mm, cm, m, in, ft.
- If the drawing prints a measurement in feet and inches (for example 3'-0"), convert it to inches and report unit 'in'. So 3'-0" becomes value 36 and unit 'in'.
- If a measurement is printed without any unit, infer the unit from the sheet's dimension convention (a note such as ALL DIMENSIONS IN MILLIMETRES, or the magnitude itself) and report that unit. A bare 900 on a metric residential plan is 900 mm.
- If you cannot read a measurement confidently, set both 'value' and 'unit' to null rather than guessing. A null is correct; an invented number is a compliance failure.

Coverage rules:
- Door and room schedules are tables, usually on their own sheet. Extract every row, not a sample. Long tables must be reported in full.
- A door that appears both on the floor plan and in the door schedule is one door. Prefer the schedule's width, because it is the authoritative dimension.
- Corridors and egress paths are often unlabelled. Report them using the nearest room names or grid references so a reviewer can find them again.
- Report the occupancy classification and building type only if the sheet states them explicitly, for example in the title block, the code-analysis block, or a general note. Do not infer them from the look of the plan.
- Put any code-related text you cannot map to a field into plan_notes: fire ratings, occupant loads, general notes, code-analysis blocks, and title-block text.

occupancy_classification.description: The building occupancy classification exactly as printed on the sheet, usually in the title block or a code-analysis block. Alberta drawings typically state a National Building Code group and division such as 'Group C' or 'Group A, Division 2'. Return the printed text verbatim. Return null if the sheet does not state it.

building_type.description: The building type or project description as printed on the sheet, for example 'single detached dwelling', 'secondary suite', or 'multi-unit residential'. Usually appears in the title block or project information block. Return null if the sheet does not state it.

rooms.description: Every named room, space, or area label on the sheet. Include unfinished and service spaces such as MECH., STORAGE, and CRAWL SPACE. One entry per room label on the drawing.

room_name.description: The room label exactly as printed on the plan, for example 'BEDROOM 2' or 'RECREATION RM.'. Preserve the drawing's capitalization and abbreviations.

room_width.description: The smaller of the two printed plan dimensions for this room. Only use dimensions printed on the drawing.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

room_length.description: The larger of the two printed plan dimensions for this room. Only use dimensions printed on the drawing.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

room_floor_area.description: The floor area if it is printed on the drawing or listed in a room schedule. Do not multiply width by length to produce this; report null unless an area is actually printed.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

unit.description: Area unit: 'm' means square metres, 'ft' means square feet.

ceiling_height.description: The finished ceiling height for this room if printed on the sheet or in a section or note that names this room. Report null when no height is given for this specific room.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

doors.description: Every door on the sheet, from both the floor plan and the door schedule. Extract every row of a door schedule, not a sample. When the same door appears in both places, report it once using the schedule's dimensions.

door_label.description: The door tag or identifier as printed, for example 'D-1' or '101A'. If the door has no tag, describe its location using the rooms it connects, for example 'bedroom 2 to hallway'.

door_clear_width.description: The door leaf or clear opening width. On a door schedule this is the width column. Prefer the schedule value over a value scaled off the plan.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

door_height.description: The door height, normally the height column of the door schedule.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

door_type.description: The door type as printed, for example 'swing', 'sliding', 'bi-fold', 'exterior', or a fire rating such as '20 min'. Return null if the sheet does not state a type.

is_exterior_door.description: True when the drawing or schedule marks this door as an exterior door, for example a type of EXT or a location on the building envelope. Null when the sheet does not make this clear.

corridors.description: Every corridor, hallway, or circulation space with a printed width. Corridors are frequently unlabelled, so identify them by the rooms or grid lines they run between.

corridor_location.description: Where this corridor is, described so a reviewer can find it again on the sheet, for example 'hallway between bedroom 2 and bathroom' or 'corridor on grid line C'.

corridor_clear_width.description: The printed clear width of the corridor, wall face to wall face.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

corridor_length.description: The printed length of the corridor along its direction of travel.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

stairs.description: Every stair and its printed geometry. Stair dimensions usually appear on the plan next to the stair run, or in a stair section or detail. One entry per stair.

stair_location.description: Which stair this is, for example 'S-1', 'stair to basement', or 'main stair between first and second floor'.

stair_clear_width.description: The clear width of the stair between walls or handrails, as printed.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

riser_height.description: The height of a single riser, not the total rise of the flight. Drawings often print this as 'RISE' or as a count such as '14 RISERS @ 190'. In that example the riser height is 190. If only a total rise and a riser count are given, report null rather than dividing.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

tread_run.description: The run or going of a single tread, not the total run of the flight. Drawings label this 'RUN', 'GOING', or 'TREAD'.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

headroom_height.description: The clear headroom over the stair if printed, usually on a stair section.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

riser_count.description: The number of risers in the flight if the drawing states it, for example from a note reading '14 RISERS @ 190'. Return null if no count is printed.

egress_paths.description: Every marked means of egress or exit route on the sheet: exit arrows, egress width callouts, travel-distance dimensions, and exit discharge notes. Report only routes the drawing actually marks; do not trace your own route through the plan.

path_origin.description: Where the marked egress route starts, using the printed room name or label, for example 'bedroom 1'.

path_destination.description: Where the marked egress route ends, for example 'exterior door at front entry' or 'exit stair S-1'.

path_clear_width.description: The clear width of the egress route if the drawing prints one.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

travel_distance.description: The travel distance along this route if the drawing prints one, commonly labelled 'TRAVEL DISTANCE' or 'T.D.'. Report null unless a distance is printed.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

dimensions.description: Every other printed dimension on the sheet that does not already belong to a room, door, corridor, stair, or egress path above. This includes window sizes, ceiling heights, guard and handrail heights, landing sizes, and wall thicknesses. Do not repeat a measurement already reported in another field.

dimension_element.description: What this dimension measures, in the drawing's own words, for example 'guard height at deck', 'window W-3 rough opening', or 'basement ceiling height'.

value.description: Numeric magnitude only, no unit characters.

plan_notes.description: Code-relevant text on the sheet that does not map to any field above: general notes, code-analysis blocks, fire-resistance ratings, occupant loads, spatial separation notes, and title-block text. One entry per note. Copy the text as printed.
